newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Review ordered on Telstra directory fee.
newsitem.headline: Review ordered on Telstra directory fee.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston on Wednesday ordered the country's chief competition watchdog to examine state telecoms carrier Telstra Corp's plans to charge for directory assistance.
Telstra, facing a newly deregulated telecommunications industry, has sought approval to charge for some previously free calls from customers asking for telephone numbers.
In return, Telstra will cut annual line rental fees by A$5.40 and said 80 percent of customers would be better off under its proposal, Alston said in a statement.
Alston can disallow the proposal, but only after an inquiry by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
"I am forwarding Telstra's proposal to the ACCC for its independent analysis and review," Alston said.

"This will enable an independent assessment of the extent to which the proposal addresses community concerns, particularly in relation to consumers in rural and regional Australia and other disadvantaged groups."

Telstra wants to be allowed to charge a A$0.50 fee for so-called "non-genuine" directory assistance calls -- inquiries where the customer could reasonably have been expected to find the number themselves.
The government plans to float off one-third of Telstra later this year to raise at least A$8 billion.
